definition_en: a small device used for doing arithmetic
core_image: 桌上按键发亮的袖珍机器
scene: 考场里只允许带一支笔。He checked the numbers on his calculator.
sceneCN: 这里 calculator 是「计算器」（第 1 个义项：做算术的电子器具）；句意是他用计算器核对数字。

senses.title: The device for arithmetic

definition_en: a chart showing the days, weeks and months of a year
core_image: 挂在墙上划满格子的纸
scene: 新年第一天她把旧的那本取下来。She marked the date on the new calendar.
sceneCN: 这里 calendar 是「日历」（第 1 个义项：按日月排列的表格）；句意是她在新日历上标出了日期。

derivatives.zh: 历法的，与日历有关的
日程表，语义相关的安排表

senses.title: The printed chart of days
senses.definition: a sheet or book showing the days and months of a year
senses.definitionCN: 印有全年日月日期的纸页或册子
senses.example: She marked the date on the new calendar.
senses.exampleCN: 她在新日历上标出了日期。
senses.why: The core image is a grid of squares hung on a wall.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是挂在墙上、由方格组成的纸。

senses.title: A system for dividing the year
senses.definition: a system that fixes the length and order of months and years

senses.title: A list of planned events
senses.definition: a list of dates on which events will happen

definition_en: to speak to someone on the phone or to say a name loudly
core_image: 举起手机喊出一个名字
scene: 深夜她想起还有件事没说。She called her mother before bed.
sceneCN: 这里 call 是「打电话」（第 1 个义项：用电话联系某人）；句意是她睡前给母亲打了电话。

derivatives.zh: 打电话的人，来访者
使命，天职；也指呼喊

senses.title: To telephone someone
senses.definition: to speak to someone by phone
senses.definitionCN: 通过电话与某人交谈
senses.example: She called her mother before bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她睡前给母亲打了电话。
senses.why: The core image is raising a phone and calling a name.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是举起手机，喊出一个名字。

senses.title: To give someone a name
senses.definition: to give a name or title to a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 给人或事物一个名称或称号
senses.example: They call the dog Lucky.
senses.exampleCN: 他们管这只狗叫 Lucky。

senses.title: To shout or cry out
senses.definition: to say something loudly so others hear

senses.example: He called for help from the shore.

senses.title: To visit briefly
senses.definition: to make a short visit to a person or place
senses.definitionCN: 短暂地拜访某人或某地

senses.exampleCN: 我明天会去拜访你。

senses.whyCN: 在门口报上自己，也算一种喊话。

definition_en: not worried, angry or excited
core_image: 无风时平整如镜的海面
scene: 暴风雨刚过，海面重新变得平滑。The sea grew calm after the storm.

senses.title: Still, without wind or waves
senses.definition: of water or weather, still and without strong movement
senses.definitionCN: 水面或天气静止、没有强烈活动
senses.example: The sea grew calm after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨后海面平静下来。

senses.why: The same object is scaled down for celebration, and the flame becomes a wish rather than a lamp.
senses.whyCN: 同一个物体被缩小用在庆祝场合，火光的作用从照明变成了许愿，于是长出了「生日蜡烛」这个义项。

intro.en: Candle has travelled almost unchanged in meaning from Latin to modern English, always naming a wax light.
intro.cn: candle 从拉丁语到现代英语，意思几乎没有变，始终指「蜡制的光源」。

items.en: candela meant a light, a torch, or a candle made of tallow, and came from candere, to shine.
items.cn: candela 指「光、火把、兽脂蜡烛」，来自 candere（发光、烧得发白）。

items.en: The word entered Old English as candel, borrowed from Latin by way of the church, where candles were used in services.
items.cn: 这个词以 candel 的形式进入古英语，是教会从拉丁语借来的，因为仪式中要用蜡烛。

items.en: Middle English kept candel and also used candelstick for the holder, showing the word had entered daily household life.
items.cn: 中古英语沿用 candel，并用 candelstick 指烛台，说明这个词已进入日常家居生活。

items.en: Printers fixed the modern spelling candle, and the compound candlelight appears in writing from this period.
items.cn: 印刷商把拼写固定为现代的 candle，candlelight 这样的复合词也在这个时期进入书面语。

items.en: Today candle names the object itself and, in compounds, the light it gives, as in candlelight and candlelit dinners.
items.cn: 今天 candle 指物体本身，也用在复合词里指它发出的光，如烛光与烛光晚餐。

note.en: Candle belongs to a small Latin family of light words and sits beside other portable lights.
note.cn: candle 属于拉丁语「光」词族，同时也和别的便携光源词相邻。

entries.definition: the SI base unit of luminous intensity
entries.definitionCN: 坎德拉，国际单位制中的发光强度单位，与 candle 同出拉丁语 candela。

entries.definition: a holder for a candle
entries.definitionCN: 烛台，由 candle 与 stick 复合而成。

entries.definition: a large branched holder for several candles
entries.definitionCN: 多枝大烛台，同样来自拉丁语 candela。

entries.definition: a stick with burning material at one end, used for light
entries.definitionCN: 火把，靠燃烧端部发光的便携光源。

entries.definition: a device that gives light, usually using oil, gas, or electricity
entries.definitionCN: 灯，通常用油、燃气或电发光的照明器具。

entries.definition: a light inside a case that protects the flame
entries.definitionCN: 灯笼，把火光罩在壳里以防风的照明物。

normalIntro.en: Sound, spelling and word family all point the same way: a small light on a stick of wax.
normalIntro.cn: 读音、拼写和词族都指向同一个画面：一根蜡上顶着一点光。

normal.en: The opening can- echoes candela, the Latin word for a light.
normal.cn: 开头的 can- 呼应拉丁语 candela，意思就是「光」。

normal.en: The -dle ending makes it feel like a small household object handled every day.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -dle 让它听起来像每天都会拿在手里的小物件。

normal.en: candlelight and candlelit keep the word alive in compounds for evening scenes.
normal.cn: candlelight 与 candlelit 让这个词一直活在描写夜晚的复合词里。

normal.en: A candle has a wick, and the verb light collocates with it: light a candle.
normal.cn: 蜡烛有灯芯，常与动词 light 搭配：light a candle（点蜡烛）。

normal.en: Candles are bought by the box, which is why a box of candles is a fixed phrase.
normal.cn: 蜡烛常按盒买，所以 a box of candles 成了固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a dark room where one small flame pushes the shadows back to the walls.
abstract.cn: 想象一间黑屋，一点小火苗把影子逼回墙角。

abstract.en: The flame eats the wax: the candle spends itself to make light.
abstract.cn: 火苗吃掉蜡：蜡烛消耗自己来发光。

abstract.en: A birthday cake is a field of small flames, each one a wish waiting to be blown out.
abstract.cn: 生日蛋糕像一片小火苗的田野，每一簇都是一个等着被吹灭的愿望。

examples.en: She lit a candle and put it on the table.
examples.cn: 她点了一支蜡烛放在桌上。

examples.en: The room was lit only by candles.
examples.cn: 房间里只有烛光照着。

examples.en: He blew out the candles on his cake and made a wish.
examples.cn: 他吹灭蛋糕上的蜡烛，许了个愿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「看抖」——火苗看得见，风一吹就抖，那就是蜡烛。

root: 拉丁语 candela（光、火把、蜡烛）来自 candere（发光、烧白）；同族词有 candela、candelabrum、candor。

sensesIntro.en: One object, two uses: a light for the room and a light for a celebration.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个物体，两种用途：照亮房间的灯，和庆祝时的那簇小火。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wick burning inside a stick of wax, giving a small steady light.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯芯在蜡里燃烧，放出一小团稳定的光。

branches.en: The everyday object that lights a room when there is no electricity.
branches.cn: 日常物件，在没有电的时候照亮房间。

branches.en: The mini version on a birthday cake, where the flame stands for a wish.
branches.cn: 生日蛋糕上的迷你版本，火苗代表一个愿望。

branches.en: Compounds such as candlelight and candlelit describe the quality of that light.
branches.cn: candlelight、candlelit 这类复合词描写这种光的质感。

branches.en: Both senses share the same physical image: a small flame at the top of wax.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享同一个物理画面：蜡顶端的一小簇火。

branches.en: Blowing out the flame turns the light into a ritual moment.
branches.cn: 吹灭火苗，把光变成了一个仪式性的瞬间。

intro.en: Candle is a base noun; most of its family is built by compounding and by Latin relatives of candere.
intro.cn: candle 是基础名词，它的词族多由复合构词和 candere 的拉丁同族词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin candela and the verb candere supply the root for light words across European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 candela 与动词 candere 为欧洲多种语言提供了「光」这一词根。

items.meaning: a wax stick with a wick that burns for light
items.meaningCN: 蜡烛，带灯芯、燃烧发光的蜡制物
items.example: A candle burned on the windowsill.
She bought two boxes of candles.

items.meaning: a holder that supports a candle
items.meaningCN: 烛台，用来插放蜡烛的器具
items.example: The silver candlestick stood on the mantelpiece.

items.exampleCN: 这家餐厅提供烛光餐桌。

items.structure: Latin noun used as a unit
items.meaning: the SI unit of luminous intensity
items.meaningCN: 坎德拉，发光强度的国际单位
items.example: The lamp is rated at two hundred candelas.
items.exampleCN: 这盏灯的发光强度为两百坎德拉。
一盏多枝烛台照亮了大厅。

items.meaningCN: 坦率、光明磊落，本义与「明亮」相关

latinEntries.meaning: a light, a torch, a candle

definition_en: a sweet food made mainly of sugar, often eaten as a treat
core_image: 一小块糖在舌尖化开，甜味立刻散满口腔
scene: 孩子把口袋里的糖分给身边的同伴。The child shared the candy in his pocket with the friends beside him.
sceneCN: 这里 candy 是「糖果」（第 1 个义项：以糖为主的甜食）；句意是孩子把口袋里的糖分给身边的同伴。

derivatives.zh: candy 加 -ed 构成，义为「糖渍的、裹糖的」
candy 与 floss 复合，英式说法，义为「棉花糖」
candy 与 maker 复合，义为「糖果制造商」

senses.title: A sweet food made of sugar
senses.definition: a small sweet food made mainly of sugar, often colored or flavored
senses.definitionCN: 以糖为主料、常加色素或香精的小块甜食
senses.example: The children were given candy after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭后孩子们得到了糖果。
senses.why: The word came through French and Arabic from a Persian term for crystallized sugar.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经法语和阿拉伯语而来，源头是波斯语里「结晶的糖」，所以最核心的意思就是糖做的甜食。

senses.title: Fruit preserved in sugar
senses.definition: fruit or peel cooked and coated in sugar so that it keeps
senses.definitionCN: 用糖煮过或裹糖保存的水果、果皮
senses.example: The shop sells candied orange peel and other candy.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖糖渍橙皮和其他蜜饯。
senses.why: Preserving fruit in sugar is the old craft behind the word, and the noun still names the result.
senses.whyCN: 用糖保存水果是这个词背后古老的工艺，名词至今仍指这样做出的成品。

intro.en: Candy reached English along the sugar trade, and every stage of the journey left a trace in the word.
intro.cn: candy 沿着糖的贸易路线进入英语，路上每一站都在词形里留下痕迹。

items.en: khanda meant a piece of sugar, a fragment of crystallized cane juice.
items.cn: khanda 指「一块糖」，即甘蔗汁结晶后的小块。

items.en: qand named cane sugar itself, and the word travelled with the sweet through Persian-speaking traders.
items.cn: qand 指甘蔗糖本身，这个词随糖一起经过波斯语商人之手。

items.en: qandi described sugar that had been crystallized, and Arabic carried the term west along trade routes.
items.cn: qandi 指结晶的糖，阿拉伯语沿商路把这个词带向西方。

items.en: sucre candi entered Old French as the name of crystallized sugar, later shortened in everyday speech.
items.cn: sucre candi 作为「结晶糖」的名称进入古法语，后来在日常口语里被缩短。

items.en: English borrowed the short form as candy, and by the nineteenth century it named sweets of many kinds.
items.cn: 英语借入缩短后的形式 candy，到十九世纪已泛指各种糖果。

note.en: Candy has no Latin root; its nearest relatives are other words for sweets and for sugar itself.
note.cn: candy 没有拉丁词根，它最近的亲戚是别的「甜食」词和「糖」本身的词。

entries.definition: preserved or coated in sugar
entries.definitionCN: 糖渍的、裹糖的，由 candy 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: spun sugar sold on a stick at fairs
entries.definitionCN: 棉花糖，candy 与 floss 复合，英式说法。

entries.definition: a small piece of sweet food made of sugar
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语里的「糖果」，与 candy 同义。

entries.definition: a sweet food made with sugar and often fruit or nuts
entries.definitionCN: 精致甜食，常含糖、水果或坚果。

entries.definition: a sweet brown food made from cocoa beans
entries.definitionCN: 巧克力，由可可豆制成的甜食。

entries.definition: the sweet course eaten at the end of a meal
entries.definitionCN: 餐后甜点，正餐结束时吃的甜食。

normalIntro.en: The spelling is simple, and the history leaves a sweet trail from Sanskrit to English.
normalIntro.cn: 拼写简单，词源则给它留下一条从梵语到英语的甜味轨迹。

normal.en: The opening can- has the same shape as cane, the plant that gives sugar.
normal.cn: 开头的 can- 与 cane（甘蔗）同一形状，正是产糖的植物。

normal.en: candied keeps the same stem and means coated in sugar.
normal.cn: candied 保留同一个词干，意思是「裹了糖的」。

normal.en: candyfloss and candy bar show the word combining freely with other nouns.
normal.cn: candyfloss 和 candy bar 说明这个词能自由地和其他名词组合。

normal.en: American English says candy where British English often says sweets.
normal.cn: 美式英语说 candy，英式英语常说 sweets。

normal.en: The plural candies simply swaps y for ies, like many nouns ending in a consonant plus y.
normal.cn: 复数 candies 只是把 y 变成 ies，和许多「辅音加 y」结尾的名词一样。

abstract.en: Picture a paper bag of colored sweets rattling in a child's pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一个彩纸糖袋在孩子口袋里哗啦作响。

abstract.en: Sugar crystals are tiny pieces of rock that melt on the tongue.
abstract.cn: 糖的结晶像极小的石块，在舌头上化掉。

abstract.en: A single candy is a small reward handed over for good behavior.
abstract.cn: 一颗糖就是为乖巧表现递过去的小奖励。

examples.en: The child shared the candy in his pocket with his friends.
examples.cn: 孩子把口袋里的糖分给了朋友。

examples.en: She bought a bag of candies for the party.
examples.cn: 她为聚会买了一袋糖果。

examples.en: Too much candy is bad for your teeth.
examples.cn: 吃太多糖对牙齿不好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「看地」——糖掉在地上，孩子低头看地找那颗糖。

root: 源流一般追溯到梵语 khanda（糖块），经波斯语 qand、阿拉伯语 qandi、古法语 sucre candi，英语缩为 candy；无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: The noun covers both sugar sweets and fruit preserved in sugar, two sides of the same sweet craft.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词既指糖做的甜食，也指用糖保存的水果，是同一门制糖手艺的两面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small piece of crystallized sugar melting on the tongue.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小块结晶的糖在舌头上化开。

branches.en: The everyday sweet sold in bars, bags, and stores.
branches.cn: 日常的甜食，成条、成袋、在店里出售。

branches.en: The older craft sense: fruit cooked in sugar so that it keeps.
branches.cn: 更古老的工艺义：用糖煮水果以便保存。

branches.en: Compounds such as candy bar and cotton candy name particular shapes of the treat.
branches.cn: candy bar、cotton candy 这类复合词指特定形状的甜食。

branches.en: Both senses rest on one image: sugar turning liquid into crystal or coating.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在同一画面上：糖把液体变成结晶或糖衣。

branches.en: In British English the same idea is usually carried by sweet.
branches.cn: 在英式英语里，同一个概念通常用 sweet 来表达。

intro.en: Candy is a borrowed base noun; its family is built by compounding and by the -ed adjective candied.
intro.cn: candy 是借入的基础名词，词族靠复合构词和 -ed 形容词 candied 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The word itself has no Latin root: the sugar trade brought it through Persian and Arabic, while Medieval Latin saccharum named sugar separately.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词本身没有拉丁词根：糖的贸易让它经波斯语、阿拉伯语传来，而中世纪拉丁语另用 saccharum 指糖。

items.meaning: a sweet food made of sugar
items.example: The jar was full of candy.
Candied ginger is served after dinner.

items.meaningCN: 棉花糖，缠在棍上的拉丝糖
items.example: The fair sold candyfloss and balloons.
items.exampleCN: 集市上卖棉花糖和气球。

items.meaning: a person or company that makes candy
items.example: The candymaker invented a new flavor.
items.exampleCN: 这家糖果厂发明了一种新口味。

items.meaning: the sweet substance from which candy is made
items.meaningCN: 糖，制作糖果的甜味原料
items.example: The recipe needs two cups of sugar.

items.meaning: the ordinary sugar used in food
items.meaningCN: 蔗糖，食品中常用的普通糖
items.example: Sucrose is broken down into simpler sugars.
items.exampleCN: 蔗糖会被分解成更简单的糖。

items.meaningCN: 糖，中世纪拉丁语对糖的称呼
items.exampleCN: saccharum 是从阿拉伯语进入拉丁语的。

definition_en: the negative form of can, used to say that something is impossible or not allowed
core_image: 伸出去的手被一堵看不见的墙挡住
scene: 门锁着，钥匙也丢了，几个人只能站在门外。The door was locked and the key was lost, so they cannot get in.
sceneCN: 这里 cannot 是「不能」（第 1 个义项：表示没有能力或条件做到）；句意是门锁着、钥匙也丢了，他们进不去。

derivatives.zh: cannot 的肯定形式，义为「能、可以」
语义对应的形容词，义为「不能的、无能力的」
语义对应的形容词，义为「无能力的、不能胜任的」

senses.title: To be unable to do something
senses.definition: used to say that someone or something is unable to do something
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人或某物没有能力做到某事
senses.example: I cannot lift this box on my own.
senses.exampleCN: 我一个人抬不起这个箱子。
senses.why: cannot is simply can plus not: the word of ability carries the meaning and not reverses it.
senses.whyCN: cannot 就是 can 加 not：表示能力的词承担意义，not 把它翻转成否定。

senses.title: To be forbidden or impossible
senses.definition: used to say that something is not allowed or is impossible
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事不被允许或不可能发生
senses.example: You cannot park your car here.
senses.exampleCN: 你不能把车停在这里。
senses.why: English negation covers both inability and prohibition, so one form serves both uses.
senses.whyCN: 英语的否定既覆盖「做不到」，也覆盖「不许做」，所以同一个形式承担两种用法。

intro.en: cannot is not a borrowed word but a join: the old verb can fused with the negative not.
intro.cn: cannot 不是借来的词，而是拼接出来的：古老的动词 can 与否定词 not 合成一体。

items.en: cunnan meant to know or to know how, and it is the ancestor of modern can.
items.cn: cunnan 意为「知道、懂得」，是现代 can 的祖先。

items.en: The negative was written as two words, can not, with not coming from nāwiht, no thing.
items.cn: 否定形式写作两个词 can not，其中的 not 来自 nāwiht（无物）。

items.en: Printers joined the two words into cannot, and the single form spread through written English.
items.cn: 印刷商把两个词合成 cannot，这个单词形式在书面英语中传开。

items.en: The contraction can't became normal in speech, while cannot stayed the careful written form.
items.cn: 缩略形式 can't 在口语中成为常态，而 cannot 保持为正式的书面形式。

items.en: Today cannot is one word and covers both inability and prohibition.
items.cn: 今天 cannot 是一个词，同时表示「做不到」和「不许做」。

note.en: cannot is a fused form, so its look-alikes are the pieces it was made from and its contraction.
note.cn: cannot 是融合形式，所以形近词就是组成它的部件和它的缩略式。

entries.definition: the positive modal used for ability and permission
entries.definitionCN: 肯定形式的模态动词，表示能力或许可，是 cannot 的基础词。

entries.definition: the usual spoken contraction of cannot
entries.definitionCN: cannot 在口语中的常用缩略形式。

entries.definition: the word that makes a clause negative
entries.definitionCN: 使句子变成否定的否定词，是 cannot 的后半部分。

entries.definition: not able to do something
entries.definitionCN: 不能做到的，语义与「不能」相近。

entries.definition: lacking the ability or qualities needed
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏所需能力或素质的。

entries.definition: not able to happen or be done
entries.definitionCN: 不可能发生或做到的，对应「不可能」这一用法。

entries.definition: not allowed by a rule or law
entries.definitionCN: 被规则或法律禁止的，对应「不可以」这一用法。

normalIntro.en: There is nothing to decode here: cannot is can and not written as one word.
normalIntro.cn: 这里不需要拆解词根：cannot 就是把 can 和 not 写成一个词。

normal.en: can plus not gives the meaning directly: ability plus negation.
normal.cn: can 加 not 直接给出意义：能力加上否定。

normal.en: The form has no space, which marks it as the formal written choice.
normal.cn: 词中间没有空格，这使它成为正式的书面选择。

normal.en: Speech usually shortens it to can't, while writing keeps cannot.
normal.cn: 口语通常缩成 can't，书面语则保留 cannot。

normal.en: Fixed phrases such as cannot help doing show the negation working inside a pattern.
normal.cn: cannot help doing 这类固定搭配展示了否定在句型里的作用。

normal.en: A bare verb follows it: cannot go, never cannot to go.
normal.cn: 它后面直接跟动词原形：cannot go，而不是 cannot to go。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching for something and stopping against invisible glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸过去，却被看不见的玻璃挡住。

abstract.en: Picture a red light at a doorway, with your feet stopped at the line.
abstract.cn: 想象门口亮着红灯，脚步停在线外。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence with the words can do crossed out and rewritten as cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话里的「能做到」被划掉，改写成「做不到」。

examples.en: I cannot lift this box on my own.
examples.cn: 我一个人抬不起这个箱子。

examples.en: You cannot park your car here.
examples.cn: 你不能把车停在这里。

examples.en: She cannot come to the meeting tomorrow.
examples.cn: 她明天不能来参加会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「看诺特」——门口挂着 no 的牌子，看见就知道不能进。

root: cannot 是 can 与 not 的合写：can 源自古英语 cunnan（知道、懂得），not 源自古英语 nāwiht（无物）。

sensesIntro.en: One negative form serves two jobs: a lack of ability and a rule that forbids.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个否定形式承担两项工作：能力上的不足，和规则上的禁止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand stopped by an invisible wall just before it reaches the thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：手在快要够到东西时被一堵看不见的墙挡住。

branches.en: The plain inability sense: the strength or skill is not there.
branches.cn: 最基本的能力不足义：力气或技能不具备。

branches.en: Both senses share can plus not, and only the source of the block differs.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享 can 加 not 的结构，区别只在「阻挡者」不同。

branches.en: Public signs use cannot to state what visitors are not allowed to do.
branches.cn: 公共标识用 cannot 说明访客不许做什么。

branches.en: In writing, cannot signals a careful, formal register compared with can't.
branches.cn: 在书面语里，cannot 相比 can't 显得更谨慎、更正式。

intro.en: cannot is a compound of two native words rather than a prefixed or suffixed form.
intro.cn: cannot 是两个本族词的复合，而不是加前缀或后缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Germanic, so there is no Latin root to list for this word.

definition_en: a soft head covering, or a cover that fits on the top of something
core_image: 一个圆顶的东西扣在头顶或瓶口上
scene: 他走进教室时把头上的帽子摘了下来。He took off his cap as he walked into the classroom.
sceneCN: 这里 cap 是「帽子」（第 1 个义项：有帽檐的软帽）；句意是他走进教室时把帽子摘了下来。

derivatives.zh: cap 加 -ful 构成，义为「一帽之量」
cap 加 -ed 构成，义为「带盖的、有上限的」
un- 加 cap 构成，义为「打开盖子」

senses.title: A soft hat with a peak
senses.definition: a soft hat with a stiff part at the front to shade the eyes
senses.definitionCN: 前部有硬檐、可以遮住眼睛的软帽
senses.example: He wore a blue cap and a light jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 他戴着一顶蓝帽，穿一件薄外套。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a covering for the head, borrowed from Latin cappa, a hood.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「头上覆盖物」，借自拉丁语 cappa（头巾）。

senses.title: A cover for the top of something
senses.definition: a cover that fits over the top of a bottle, pen, or tube
senses.definitionCN: 盖在瓶子、笔或管子顶端的罩子
senses.example: Put the cap back on the bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 把瓶盖重新盖上。
senses.why: If a cap sits on a head, the same shape sits on a bottle, so the word moved to covers.
senses.whyCN: 既然帽是扣在头上的，同样的形状扣在瓶口上，词义就自然延伸到「盖子」。

senses.title: An upper limit
senses.definition: the highest amount that is allowed or possible
senses.definitionCN: 被允许或可能达到的最高数额
senses.example: The government set a cap on energy prices.
senses.exampleCN: 政府为能源价格设定了上限。
senses.why: A cover marks the top of a container, and a limit marks the top of a range, so cap came to mean ceiling.
senses.whyCN: 盖子是容器的顶端，限额是一个范围的顶端，于是 cap 又引申为「天花板、上限」。

intro.en: Cap began as a word for a hood and slowly moved from heads to bottle tops and to limits.
intro.cn: cap 最初指「头巾」，后来从头上移到瓶口，再引申为「上限」。

items.en: cappa named a hood or a cloak with a hood, probably from a pre-Latin Mediterranean source.
items.cn: cappa 指「头巾、带帽的斗篷」，可能来自拉丁语之前的某地中海语言。

items.en: Old English borrowed it as cæppe, naming a hood or a head covering.
items.cn: 古英语借入为 cæppe，指头巾或头部覆盖物。

items.en: cap settled into everyday use for a close-fitting head covering worn by workers and soldiers.
items.cn: 中古英语里 cap 稳定指工人和士兵戴的贴身帽。

items.en: The sense extended to covers that sit on top of objects, such as the cap of a bottle.
items.cn: 词义扩展到盖在物体顶端的覆盖物，例如瓶盖。

items.en: From the idea of a top piece came the abstract sense of an upper limit, as in a cap on prices.
items.cn: 从「顶端部件」这个想法里长出了抽象义「上限」，例如价格上限。

note.en: Cap shares its root with cape, and its meanings spread from headwear to lids and limits.
note.cn: cap 与 cape 同源，词义从头饰扩展到盖子，再到上限。

entries.definition: a sleeveless cloak, or a point of land
entries.definitionCN: 无袖斗篷，也指海角；与 cap 同出拉丁语 cappa。

entries.definition: the greatest amount that is allowed
entries.definitionCN: 允许的最大数量，对应 cap 的第三个义项。

normalIntro.cn: 拼写很短，围绕它的词族正好展示了词义的每一站。

normal.en: cape and cap are cousins, both from Latin cappa, a hooded cloak.

abstract.en: Picture a cap shading a pair of eyes on a bright day.
abstract.cn: 想象大太阳下，帽檐替一双眼睛挡住光。

sensesIntro.en: One shape, three places: on a head, on a bottle, and on the top of a range of numbers.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个形状用在三处：头上、瓶口上，以及一串数字的顶端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round cover dropped onto the top of something.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个圆形的覆盖物扣在某物的顶端。

branches.en: The clothing sense: a soft hat that shades the eyes.
branches.cn: 衣物义：遮挡眼睛的软帽。

branches.en: The container sense: a small lid on a bottle or pen.
branches.cn: 容器义：瓶口或笔端的小盖子。

branches.en: The abstract sense: a highest allowed amount.
branches.cn: 抽象义：被允许的最高数额。

branches.en: Both the lid and the limit sit on top and stop something from going further.
branches.cn: 盖子和上限都位于顶端，都阻止某物继续外溢或上升。

branches.en: As a verb, cap means to put that ceiling in place.
branches.cn: 作动词时，cap 指把这个天花板设好。

intro.en: Cap is a short base noun that also works as a verb; its family grows with -ed, -ful, and un-.
intro.cn: cap 是简短的基础名词，也可作动词；词族靠 -ed、-ful 和 un- 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin cappa, a hooded cloak, is the source of cap and of several words for head coverings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cappa（带帽斗篷）是 cap 以及多个「头饰」词的来源。

definition_en: having the ability or skill needed to do something
core_image: 一个人挽起袖子，双手稳稳接住递过来的任务
scene: 她一个人就能把这项工作做完。She is capable of finishing the work on her own.

senses.title: Having the skill to do something
senses.definition: able to do something well because of skill or experience
senses.definitionCN: 因具备技能或经验而能把事情做好
senses.example: She is a capable manager who solves problems quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位能干的经理，解决问题很快。
senses.why: Latin capere means to take or hold, so capable describes someone who can take a task in hand.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 capere 意为「抓住、握住」，所以 capable 描写的是能把任务稳稳接在手里的人。

senses.title: Able to do or experience something
senses.definition: having the qualities or conditions needed for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 具备让某事发生所需要的性质或条件
senses.example: The material is capable of holding a great deal of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这种材料能够储存大量热量。
senses.why: The idea of holding widens from people to things, so capable of can describe what an object can do.
senses.whyCN: 「容纳、握住」的想法从人扩展到物，所以 capable of 也能说明一个物体能做到什么。

intro.en: Capable comes from a Latin verb for taking hold, and its history explains why it pairs with of.
intro.cn: capable 来自拉丁语中表示「抓住」的动词，这段历史也解释了它为什么常与 of 搭配。

items.en: capere meant to take, to seize, or to hold, and it supplies the root cap-.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿、抓、容纳」，提供了 cap- 这个词根。

items.en: capabilis was formed to mean able to hold or able to receive.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语造出 capabilis，意为「能容纳的、能接受的」。

items.en: The adjective passed into Old French as capable with the same sense of being fit to receive.
items.cn: 这个形容词以 capable 进入古法语，仍表示「能够接受、容纳」。

items.en: English borrowed it to describe a person or thing able to take in or undertake something.
items.cn: 英语借入后，用它描写能够接纳或承担某事的人或物。

items.en: The modern sense focuses on skill and ability, and the pattern be capable of became fixed.
items.cn: 现代义集中在技能与能力上，be capable of 的搭配也固定下来。

note.en: Capable sits in a large Latin family built on capere, and it is close in meaning to able and competent.
note.cn: capable 处在以 capere 为基础的大词族里，语义上又接近 able 与 competent。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands taking hold of a task and holding it without dropping it.

branches.en: The personal sense: a person with the skill to handle work.

branches.en: The extended sense: a thing with the properties needed for an effect.
branches.cn: 扩展义：具备产生某种效果所需性质的物。

branches.en: Both senses keep the original image of holding something within reach.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留着「把东西握在可及之处」的原始画面。

branches.en: In appraisal, capable is a solid compliment without the force of brilliant.

senses.title: The amount a container can hold
senses.definition: the maximum amount that a container, room, or vehicle can hold

senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅能容纳五百人就座。

senses.title: The ability to do or understand something
senses.definition: the mental or physical power to do, learn, or understand something
senses.definitionCN: 做事、学习或理解某事的脑力或体力
senses.example: Children have a remarkable capacity for learning languages.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们学习语言的能力惊人。
senses.why: If the mind is a container, what it can take in is also its capacity.
senses.whyCN: 如果把头脑看成一个容器，它能装进去的东西，自然也被称为 capacity。

senses.title: The maximum amount a factory can produce
senses.definition: the largest amount that a factory, machine, or system can produce in a period
senses.definitionCN: 工厂、机器或系统在一段时间内能产出的最大数量
senses.example: The plant is working at full capacity this month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂本月正满负荷生产。

intro.en: Capacity is the noun of holding: it comes from the Latin adjective for roomy.
intro.cn: capacity 是「容纳」的名词形式，来自拉丁语中表示「能装」的形容词。

items.en: capax meant able to hold or roomy, built on capere, to take or hold.

items.en: capacitas turned that adjective into a noun naming the power to hold.

items.en: English borrowed it for the volume a vessel could contain.

entries.definitionCN: 做事的能力或技能，对应第二个义项。

entries.definition: the power or skill to do something
entries.definitionCN: 能力、性能，与 capacity 在「能力」义上接近。

entries.definition: the amount that is produced
entries.definitionCN: 产出的数量，对应「产能」这一义项。

normalIntro.en: The root cap- means to hold, and -ity makes it a noun: the holding power of a container.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 cap- 意为「容纳」，-ity 把它变成名词：容器的「容纳力」。

normal.en: cap- comes from Latin capere, to take or hold.
normal.cn: cap- 来自拉丁语 capere，意为「拿、容纳」。

normal.en: -ity turns the adjective into a noun, as in able and ability.
normal.cn: -ity 把形容词变成名词，就像 able 与 ability 的关系。

normal.en: capable and capacity are close relatives with the same stem.
normal.cn: capable 与 capacity 是同一个词干下的近亲。

normal.en: at full capacity is the fixed phrase for a place or machine working to its limit.
normal.cn: at full capacity 是固定说法，指场所或机器满负荷运转。

normal.en: The plural capacities simply changes y to ies.
normal.cn: 复数 capacities 只是把 y 变成 ies。

abstract.en: Picture a glass filled to the very edge, with one more drop ready to spill.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子被灌到杯沿，再一滴就要溢出。

abstract.en: Picture a head with shelves inside, each shelf waiting to be filled with knowledge.
abstract.cn: 想象头脑里有一层层架子，等着被知识填满。

abstract.en: Picture a factory running all night, every machine busy at once.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂通宵运转，每台机器同时开足。

examples.en: The tank has a capacity of one hundred litres.
examples.cn: 这个水箱能装一百升水。

examples.en: The hall has a seating capacity of five hundred.
examples.cn: 这个大厅能容纳五百人就座。

examples.en: The plant is working at full capacity this month.
examples.cn: 这家工厂本月正满负荷生产。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可拍 city」——一座城能装下多少人，就是它的容量。

root: 拉丁语 capax（能容纳的）→ capacitas（容量）→ 古法语 capacité → 英语 capacity；词根 capere（抓住、容纳）。

sensesIntro.en: Container, mind, and factory are all treated as things with a limit to what they can hold.
sensesIntro.cn: 容器、头脑和工厂都被看成有「容纳上限」的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vessel filled slowly until the surface reaches the rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：容器被慢慢灌满，液面升到边缘。

branches.en: The physical sense: how much a tank, hall, or bus can contain.
branches.cn: 物理义：水箱、大厅或公交车能装多少。

branches.en: The mental sense: how much a person can learn or understand.
branches.cn: 心智义：一个人能学习或理解多少。

branches.en: The industrial sense: how much a plant can produce in a period.
branches.cn: 工业义：工厂在一段时间内能生产多少。

branches.en: All three senses measure a limit of holding, whether space, mind, or machine.
branches.cn: 三个义项都在度量「容纳的上限」，只是对象分别是空间、头脑和机器。

branches.en: at full capacity marks the exact point where no more can be added.
branches.cn: at full capacity 标记的正是再也装不下的那个点。

intro.en: Capacity is a noun built from the root cap- plus the noun suffix -ity.
intro.cn: capacity 是由词根 cap- 加名词后缀 -ity 构成的。

latinIntro.en: Latin capax and capacitas carry the idea of holding, from the verb capere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capax 与 capacitas 都承载「容纳」之意，源头是动词 capere。

items.meaning: the amount that can be held
items.example: The battery has a large capacity.
The two plants have similar capacities.
items.exampleCN: 这两家工厂的产能相近。

items.example: A capacious coat has deep pockets.
items.exampleCN: 宽大的外套有很深的口袋。

items.meaning: the state of being unable to do something
items.example: The injury caused a temporary incapacity.
items.exampleCN: 这次受伤造成了暂时的失能。

items.meaning: a device that stores electric charge
items.meaningCN: 电容器，储存电荷的元件
items.example: The capacitor stores energy for the flash.
items.exampleCN: 电容器为闪光灯储存能量。

items.meaning: the ability of a system to store charge
items.meaningCN: 电容，系统储存电荷的能力

items.meaning: having the ability to do something
items.example: She is capable of leading the team.
items.exampleCN: 她有能力带领这个团队。

items.meaning: to take, to hold, to contain
items.example: Capere underlies many words about holding.
items.exampleCN: capere 是许多表示「容纳」的词的底层词根。
